source_evidence: To bring your portfolio back to its original asset allocation, you may need to rebalance your portfolio.
answer: Portfolio rebalancing means adjusting your holdings to bring them back toward your original asset allocation. Because investments can grow at different rates, your portfolio may drift away from its intended mix and its risk level may change. For example, if stocks rise from 60% to 80% of your portfolio, you could sell some stocks and/or add money to other asset categories to restore the original mix. The source notes that some experts suggest rebalancing on a regular schedule or when holdings move beyond a preset percentage, and that it tends to work best when done relatively infrequently.
